source: ACIAR Monograph No. 146a, "ដំណាំសំណែកសៀង" [Soybean Growers Manual], Belfield S., Brown C., Martin M. (eds.), New South Wales Department of Primary Industries / Murdoch University / CARDI / ACIAR, 2012
text: Storage guidance covers drying seed/grain to a safe moisture content before bagging, using sun-drying on mats or concrete/tarpaulin floors with a photo showing farmers raking grain into thin layers for even drying. The manual specifically flags the bruchid weevil (Callosobruchus spp.) as the dominant storage pest risk, explaining that weevil eggs can already be present on pods at harvest and develop inside stored seed over time, so recommends: drying thoroughly before storage, using sealed/pest-proof storage containers, and treating stored seed with an approved storage protectant (aluminium sulphate is named as a fumigant/protectant option, applied at a stated rate per unit of stored grain) where bruchid pressure is high.
